newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REEVES IS FALCONS COACH, VICE PRESIDENT.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REEVES IS FALCONS COACH, VICE PRESIDENT.

text.p: Dan Reeves, fired last month as head coach of the New York Giants, was named executive vice president and head coach of the Atlanta Falcons on Monday.
Reeves, a native of Rome, Georgia, who turned 53 on Sunday, replaces June Jones, who was fired after a 3-13 season.

Reeves has won more NFL games than any other active coach, but openly feuded with Giants general manager George Young and player personnel director Tom Boisture, a battle that ultimately ended in his dismissal on December 23rd.
New York went 6-10 in 1996, posting consecutive losing seasons for the first time since 1979-80. It was the first time in Reeves' 31-year football career that had occurred.

Reeves found the level of control he was looking for in Atlanta, where he received a five-year contract and is expected to have the final say in all football related matters. Financial terms were not disclosed, but the Atlanta Journal-Constitution said the deal is worth between $7.5 and $8 million.
Reeves has a career record of 149-113-1, but went 32-34 in four years with New York.

He took the Denver Broncos to three Super Bowls but was fired in 1992 after 12 seasons in Denver, where he clashed with star quarterback John Elway. The Broncos made the playoffs six times under Reeves.
New York hired Reeves in January 1993 and went an unexpected 11-5 in his first season. The Giants won a playoff game, but were routed by San Francisco in the divisional round, 44-3.

Reeves takes over a Falcons' programme in shambles after a disastrous 1996 season that included the release of quarterback Jeff George, who argued with Jones on the sidelines in a September 22nd game against Philadelphia after being benched.
Reeves is almost certain to scrap the run-and-shoot offence employed by Jones and use a more conventional system.
Reeves was a player and an assistant coach for the Dallas Cowboys.
Bobby Ross, who coached at Georgia Tech, was believed to be the first choice of the Falcons, but Ross was hired last week by the Detroit Lions.
